Join the Ant Ling community on Discord.
Share what you build with Ling-3.2-flash, exchange ideas with other developers, and tell us what you want to see next.
https://t.co/TwbjGjpDza

Try Ling-3.2-flash on Computrix.
Bring your own images and real-world tasks, and explore what it can do.
https://t.co/bITFONMZT9

Demo: Everyday health assistance

From meal photos to a weekly food journal: Ling-3.2-flash identifies ingredients, estimates portions and uses nutrition data to estimate calories and nutrient balance, then organizes the results into an illustrated log. https://t.co/Mlq0ZTd57D

Demo: Documents into deliverables

Ling-3.2-flash reads research PDFs, including equations and diagrams, and implements the algorithms in working code. It also turns business materials into brochures, using visual previews to refine layout and spacing. https://t.co/rlDalAyMe3

Demo: 3D scenes from 2D references

From one 2D reference image, Ling-3.2-flash recreates game and simulation assets. It inspects headless renders of material spheres, compares roughness, normal maps and bump detail, and iteratively refines scripts for high-fidelity results. https://t.co/gCvNU6MV0n

Demo: Frontend design & professional tools

Ling-3.2-flash turns visual intent into responsive frontends with animation, operates Blender through UI actions and parameter changes, and turns engineering drawings into 3D models for the web. https://t.co/gRLw4lA60q

Demo: Multi-agent collaboration

Ling-3.2-flash coordinates specialist agents using shared context to turn Q2 financial data into an analysis report, a six-slide board deck and a highlights video, then refines the deliverables in response to user feedback. https://t.co/K2onjbGFlO

Ling-3.0-flash has 124B total parameters, while activating only 5.1B per token.
This work extends the same efficiency principle beyond model architecture: kernels, quantization, decoding, and hardware must work together to turn more of every unit of compute into useful intelligence.

On a synthetic workload with 32K input and 2K output tokens, the combined stack reached 102.88 tok/s—+185.1% over the baseline.
But this is workload-specific. On GSM8K, MTP accepted 2.68 tokens per round, versus 3.90 on the synthetic test. Real workloads must be benchmarked independently.

data.text:
On a synthetic workload with 32K input and 2K output tokens, the combined stack reached 102.88 tok/s—+185.1% over the baseline.
But this is workload-specific. On GSM8K, MTP accepted 2.68 tokens per round, versus 3.90 on the synthetic test. Real workloads must be benchmarked

Three optimizations made the difference:
1. Humming MXFP4 MoE kernels: +9.3%
2. Online FP8 LM-head quantization: +21.7% cumulatively
3. NEXTN-based MTP: drafting and verifying multiple tokens per round
The first two reduce the cost per step. MTP reduces the number of steps. https://t.co/U7S7KHuTNg

note_tweet.text:
In technical collaboration with the @NVIDIAAI  team, we optimized inference for the open-weight Ling-3.0-flash model on a single NVIDIA DGX Spark using three techniques.
Across 1,319 GSM8K questions, decode throughput increased 42.5%—from 37.81 to 53.89 tok/s—while mean latency fell 24.5%, from 15.21s to 11.49s, with no statistically detectable accuracy change. 🧵
